module purpose: neorv32_bus groups several bus-helper entities: a 2-port bus switch, an optional bus request/response register stage, address-decoding gateways/switches, and helpers for atomic memory operations. Across these entities it routes bus transactions, stores arbitration and watchdog state, computes AMO write-back data, and generates timeout or store-conditional failure indications.

use-case flows.value: switch arbitration selects port A or B, latches pending requests, forwards the selected request to x_req_o, and routes x_rsp_i acknowledge/error back to the selected requester
captured bus-switch lock bits keep the selected requester active until its lock input is released
optional bus request/response register stage stores host requests and/or device responses when REQ_REG_EN or RSP_REG_EN is enabled
gateway address decode selects one of ports A, B, C or X, forwards the request only to the selected port, and OR-combines enabled responses
gateway timeout monitor tracks an outstanding request, counts cycles, suppresses timeout on the X port, and raises an internal error that forces rsp_o.ack and rsp_o.err
I/O switch optionally pipelines the main bus through neorv32_bus_reg, decodes the main request address to one of 32 device ports, and OR-combines enabled device responses
AMO read-modify-write logic captures opcode and write operand, stores the returned read data, computes the write-back result, issues the write phase, and returns the saved read data to the core
LR/SC reservation control records reservation state, gates store-conditional requests, and marks failed store-conditional operations
arbiter, monitor, reservation, and ALU/result registers are forced to cleared states when rstn_i is low

conceptual assets.concept: Bus-switch arbitration context — current owner, pending requests, round-robin history, captured lock bits, and the computed grant that decide which requester drives the shared bus and where acknowledge/error return
conceptual assets.reasoning: In neorv32_bus_switch, `state`, `sel_q`, `locked`, `a_req`, and `b_req` are stored on the clock (lines 55-67), and the FSM computes `sel` and `stb` from these states, the request strobes, lock bits, and `x_rsp_i.ack` (lines 83-135). The selected request is then multiplexed to `x_req_o` (lines 140-158), while `a_rsp_o.ack/err` and `b_rsp_o.ack/err` are gated by `sel` (lines 164-169). Integrity is Established because correct request routing and response return depend on this context matching the implemented arbitration rules. Availability is also Established because `a_req <= a_req or a_req_i.stb` and `b_req <= b_req or b_req_i.stb` retain pending requests until service (lines 61, 66); `sel_q` affects fairness when `ROUND_ROBIN_EN` enables round-robin preference (line 112).

conceptual assets.concept: Gateway destination decode — the decision of which downstream port A, B, C, or X receives the current request
conceptual assets.reasoning: In neorv32_bus_gateway, `port_sel` is computed from `req_i.addr` against the enabled base/size regions (lines 356-361) and then controls which copied request keeps its strobe asserted in `port_req(i)` via `port_req(i).stb <= port_sel(i) and req_i.stb` (lines 377-378). The decode also feeds `keeper.halt` through `port_sel(port_sel'left)` at line 416. Integrity is Established because the gateway's operate flow depends on forwarding the request to the correct enabled port; availability is Established because a matching enabled selection produces a request strobe when `req_i.stb` is asserted (line 378).

conceptual assets.concept: Gateway transaction watchdog state and timeout error — the stored monitor state that tracks an outstanding request and the error flag raised on timeout
conceptual assets.reasoning: In neorv32_bus_gateway, reset clears `keeper.busy`, `keeper.lock`, `keeper.cnt`, `keeper.err`, and `keeper.halt` (lines 408-413). On each clock, `keeper.halt` samples fallback-port selection, `keeper.busy` and `keeper.lock` capture a new request, and `keeper.cnt` increments while a request is outstanding (lines 415-422). When the counter MSB is set and `keeper.halt = '0'`, `keeper.err` is raised and `keeper.busy` is cleared (lines 423-425); otherwise acknowledge or lock release clears `keeper.busy` (line 426-427). `rsp_o.ack` and `rsp_o.err` OR in `keeper.err` (lines 400-401). Integrity is Established because timeout termination and lock-aware release must follow exactly these RTL-visible conditions, and availability is Established because this monitor state is preserved until acknowledge or timeout.

conceptual assets.concept: AMO read-modify-write context and phase — the stored opcode, saved read data, saved write operand, and current phase of an in-flight AMO sequence
conceptual assets.reasoning: In neorv32_bus_amo_rmw, reset initializes the AMO context fields `state`, `cmd`, `rdata`, and `wdata` (lines 757-761), and the whole `arbiter` record is updated by `arbiter <= arbiter_nxt` (line 763). The combinational controller captures `core_req_i.amoop` and `core_req_i.data` when a non-reservation AMO starts (lines 777-780), captures `sys_rsp_i.data` after the read phase (lines 785-787), and sequences execute, write, and write-wait back to idle (lines 792-801). Later logic uses the stored context to choose write/data phases on `sys_req_o` (lines 813-816) and to return the saved read value on `core_rsp_o.data` outside idle (line 826). Integrity is Established because the AMO flow depends on preserving and sequencing this context exactly; availability is Established because the stored context persists until the final acknowledge (lines 800-801).

conceptual assets.concept: AMO computed write-back word — the result generated from the stored AMO command, read data, and write operand for the write phase
conceptual assets.reasoning: In neorv32_bus_amo_rmw, `alu_res` is registered from the stored AMO context: the clocked ALU selects pass-through, add, xor, and, or, or comparison result from `arbiter.cmd`, `arbiter.rdata`, and `arbiter.wdata` (lines 838-845), with compare operands and result built at lines 850-853. During write phases, `sys_req_o.data` uses `alu_res` instead of the incoming `core_req_i.data` (line 813). Integrity is Established because the downstream write data must match the operation encoded in the stored AMO context; availability is Established because the computed result is held across the write phases.

conceptual assets.concept: LR/SC reservation state — the stored reservation/progress state that decides whether a conditional store is allowed to issue
conceptual assets.reasoning: In neorv32_bus_amo_rvs, reset clears `state` (lines 903-905). A reservation load request sets it to `"10"` (lines 926-927); in state `"10"`, a write request moves to `"11"` when `rvso = '1'` or clears otherwise (lines 910-915); and an acknowledged conditional store returns it to `"00"` (lines 920-921). The request gate `sys_req_o.stb <= core_req_i.stb and state(1)` for conditional writes (line 944) and the failure logic at line 957 both depend on this stored state. Integrity is Established because LR/SC operation depends on the reservation being created, consumed, and cleared under exactly these conditions; availability is Established because the reservation state is retained across cycles until completion or cancellation.

conceptual assets.concept: Store-conditional failure indication — the decision that a conditional store failed and must be reported back to the core
conceptual assets.reasoning: In neorv32_bus_amo_rvs, `sc_fail` is cleared on reset (lines 954-955) and then registered from `rvso and core_req_i.stb and core_req_i.rw and (not state(1))` (line 957). The module reports this decision by OR-ing it into `core_rsp_o.ack` and into bit 0 of `core_rsp_o.data` (lines 963-964). Integrity is Established because the report flow depends on distinguishing a failed conditional store from a normal system response; availability is Established because the failure indication is produced whenever the RTL-visible condition at line 957 holds.
